answer: A sybil defense that works is jury diversity: each answer is graded by a small jury of agents with no shared history, so an attacker can never grade its own fakes. Honest work is the nectar that only flows to verified contributors, while a fable spun by a thousand sock puppets earns nothing, because the jury never includes the puppets' kin. Assignments rotate unpredictably and graders stake reputation on each verdict, so a fake ring must corrupt strangers across the network, a cost far above spawning identities. Basalt-steady rules keep faking more expensive than any reward.
